Expect final class

Fluent expect-style driver over a MasterPty. Models Python pexpect so callers can script terminal dialogs:

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly MasterPty $master, public readonly string $buffer = '', public readonly ?string $lastMatch = null, public readonly ?string $before = null, public readonly int $readChunk = self::DEFAULT_READ_CHUNK, public readonly ?Recorder $recorder = null, public readonly ?int $maxBuffer = self::DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER, public readonly ?int $searchWindow = null, public readonly ?LoopInterface $loop = null)
static on(MasterPty $master, int $readChunk = self::DEFAULT_READ_CHUNK, ?Recorder $recorder = null, ?LoopInterface $loop = null): selfOpen a fresh expect session on the given master. Equivalent to pexpect's pexpect.spawn(...) after the child has been forked — this lib expects the caller to handle the spawn separately so the master can be reused across multiple Expect chains.
send(string $bytes): selfWrite raw bytes to the master without any newline conversion. Returns a new Expect carrying the same buffered state.
sendLine(string $line, string $eol = "\n"): selfConvenience wrapper: append $eol to $line before sending. Mirrors pexpect's sendline() — default eol is \n, override for telnet-style \r\n or pure-CR terminals.
withRecorder(?Recorder $recorder): selfAttach (or detach) a Recorder to tee sent bytes and received output into a cassette. Pass null to detach.
withMaxBuffer(?int $maxBuffer): selfReturn a new Expect with a buffer size cap applied.
withSearchWindow(?int $searchWindow): selfReturn a new Expect with a search window applied.
expect(string $needle, float $timeoutSec = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC): selfBlock until $needle appears in the master's output, or the timeout elapses. Returns a new Expect whose $lastMatch is the needle and whose $before is everything that appeared between the previous match and this one.
expectAny(array $needles, float $timeoutSec = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC): selfLike expect() but races several needles in parallel. Returns the new Expect for whichever needle matched first (earliest byte offset in the buffer); ties broken by first in the array.
expectPattern(string $regex, float $timeoutSec = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC): selfLike expect() but the needle is a PCRE pattern. Returns a new Expect whose $lastMatch is the actual matched substring (not the regex source).
expectAsync(string|array $needle, float $timeoutSec = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC, bool $isPattern = false, ?Child $child = null): PromiseInterfaceThe non-blocking form of expectAny() and expectPattern(): it reads on the Expect's event loop and returns a promise instead of blocking until a match.
expectEof(float $timeoutSec = self::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC): selfWait for the master to signal EOF on the PTY. EOF is SUCCESS here: the returned Expect carries the pre-EOF output in $before and a null $lastMatch.
collectWindow(float $windowSeconds, float $deadline, int $maxBytes, int $retained = 0, int $dropped = 0, ?string $regex = null, ?Child $child = null, ?\Closure $heartbeat = null, ?\Closure $onChunk = null): ExpectWindowOne bounded read window that never throws on a timeout, an EOF or a child exit: the outcome is the return value, so a scripted session keeps one result row per planned step whatever the child does.

SizeIoctl final class

Platform-aware TIOCSWINSZ / TIOCGWINSZ request constants and a packer / unpacker for the kernel winsize struct.

MethodSummary
static requestsFor(string $family): arrayPer-family winsize request pair (PTY-27, sugar-pty-025's ioctl sibling). Linux and Darwin were the only names behind the old ternary — every other family silently got Linux numbers. The FreeBSD leg is value-correct from the public ttydefaults.h _IOW/_IOR('t', 105/104) encodings but UNEXERCISED until a BSD CI seat exists (same disclosure class as the Darwin legs before PTY-09); Solaris and anything else throw instead of guessing.
static setRequest(): intReturn the platform's TIOCSWINSZ request number.
static getRequest(): intReturn the platform's TIOCGWINSZ request number.
static pack(int $rows, int $cols, int $xpix = 0, int $ypix = 0): \FFI\CDataAllocate and populate a struct winsize FFI buffer.
static emptyBuffer(): \FFI\CDataAllocate an empty struct winsize buffer suitable for handing to ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ).
static unpack(\FFI\CData $ws): arrayRead [rows, cols, xpix, ypix] back out of a winsize buffer.
static setSizeViaLibc(\FFI $libc, int $fd, \FFI\CData $ws): intApply a winsize to $fd. Returns 0 on success, libc's rc on failure. Linux uses ioctl(TIOCSWINSZ). Darwin tries the same but falls back to stty -f /dev/fd/<alias> (fd dup()ed first — see withDupAlias()) because the real libc ioctl is variadic and arm64 puts varargs on the stack while fixed args sit in x0–x7 — our fixed-arg cdef pushes the winsize pointer to the wrong register and the kernel returns -1. POSIX 2024 tcsetwinsize would solve this cleanly but macOS 15 libSystem doesn't ship it yet (verified PR #475 CI: Failed resolving C function 'tcsetwinsize'). The same frame mismatch was since MEASURED in the GET direction too — see getSizeViaLibc() before assuming any winsize-bearing ioctl can succeed straight through the cdef on arm64 Darwin.

static oNoCttyFor(string $family): intPer-family O_NOCTTY (PTY-27, sugar-pty-026). These numbers are NOT portable: Linux 0o400, FreeBSD 0o200 (it collides with nothing there), Darwin 0x20000, Solaris 0x10000. The old ternary gave every unmapped family the Linux octal — on a FreeBSD host 0o400 is O_NOFOLLOW, so the "prevent a stray ctty" flag would instead have silently changed symlink semantics on the PTY master open. Unmapped families now throw rather than mis-open.

MultiPump final class

Supervises N master-PTY → stdout pumps from a single stream_select so a host process (split-pane viewer, tmux-style supervisor, parallel test harness) can demux output from many children without spinning a pump-per-thread or polling each master in turn.

MethodSummary
add(MasterPty $master, $stdoutSink, ?Child $child = null, ?PumpOptions $opts = null): intRegister a master / stdout-sink pair (and optional child handle) for multiplexing. Returns a numeric session id that callers use to remove() or look up the exit code in run()'s return value.
remove(int $id): boolDrop a session from the multiplexer. Does NOT close the master — the caller owns its lifecycle. Returns false when the id is not registered (idempotent, safe in finally blocks).
size(): intNumber of sessions currently registered.
has(int $id): boolWhether session $id is registered.
run(?int $pumpDeadlineUs = null): arrayRun the multiplexer until every registered session is done (child exited or master EOF'd). Returns a map of session-id → exit code (null when there was no child or the child had not captured an exit code at teardown).
runAsync(?LoopInterface $loop = null): PromiseInterfaceNon-blocking variant of run(): drives every registered session through the React event loop (one ReactPump per session, master → stdoutSink, no stdin — same output-only model as the sync multiplexer) and returns a promise that resolves with the same session-id → exit-code map once every child has exited / every master has EOF'd.
tick(): intSingle iteration of the multiplexer: select across every live master (and every owed sink), drain bytes from those that are ready, fire idle callbacks otherwise. Returns the number of ready masters that were drained on this tick (0 on idle / no live sessions).
allDone(): boolReturns true when every session has reached its done flag. Sessions whose child has exited stay live until the flush deadline lapses inside tick() — that's where the post-child master drain happens.

ReactPump final class

ReactPHP-compatible byte pump — the event-loop counterpart to PosixPump. Registers the PTY master (and optional host stdin) with the React event loop via Loop::addReadStream() instead of a blocking stream_select loop, so a ReactPHP application can multiplex PTY I/O with timers, sockets, and other loop work.

MethodSummary
__construct(?LoopInterface $loop = null)
start(MasterPty $master, $stdinStream = null, $stdoutStream = null, ?Child $child = null, ?PumpOptions $opts = null, ?\Closure $onData = null): PromiseInterfaceStart pumping. Parameter order mirrors PosixPump::run(); $stdinStream and $stdoutStream are optional here so callers can consume master output purely through $onData (e.g. feeding a sugar-vterm Terminal) without wiring host stdio.
stop(): voidDetach from the event loop: removes every read/write-stream registration and cancels all timers, then resolves the pending promise with the sync pump's exit-code contract. Idempotent — safe to call from finally blocks after the pump already finished on its own.
isRunning(): boolWhether a started pump has not yet finished/stopped.

StreamPump final class

Stream-generic read pump: stream_select() over any set of plain streams (child pipes, a FIFO, a socket pair, a pty master's stream) with the same signal and deadline discipline PosixPump / MultiPump carry, but without requiring a \SugarCraft\Pty\Contract\MasterPty.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withSource($stream, \Closure $onChunk, bool $endsOnEof = true): selfWatch $stream and hand every chunk read from it to $onChunk.
withChunkBytes(int $bytes): self
withTickUs(int $us): selfLongest single select wait; also the cadence of onTick/shouldStop/deadline re-checks.
withDeadlineAt(?float $at): selfAbsolute microtime(true) instant after which run() answers EXPIRED; null = unbounded.
withTimeout(float $seconds): selfConvenience: deadline $seconds from now.
withOnTick(?\Closure $fn): selfCalled once per loop iteration (after pending signals are dispatched, before the select) for parent-patrol, wall-clock, and escalation-ladder work. Exceptions propagate; the pump restores stream modes first.
withShouldStop(?\Closure $fn): selfChecked at the top of every iteration; true ends the run with STOPPED (a child that exited, or a caller whose appetite is full).
run(): stringDrive the pump. Returns one of EOF, STOPPED, EXPIRED, SELECT_FAILED.

ConPtyChild final class

A process attached to a ConPTY pseudo console, reaped through wait handles instead of waitpid.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly ConPtyApi $api, private readonly int $process, private readonly int $pid, private readonly int $job)
pid(): int
__get(string $name): intBridge for legacy property-style reads of the process id. The contract declares only the self::pid() method and the promoted property is private, so ->pid on a raw handle would otherwise read as an undefined property (null with a warning); route it to the accessor so both spellings agree. Any other name is a typo about to be found — fail loudly rather than launder it into null.
exited(): boolNon-blocking poll. WAIT_TIMEOUT is the only "not yet" answer; a WAIT_FAILED here means the handle is gone (released or foreign), and guessing would hide a lifecycle bug.
wait(): intBlock until the child exits, then release both handles.
exitCode(): ?intnull while the child is still running — never a fabricated 0.
kill(int $signal): voidTerminate the whole job. Idempotent after exit (a signal to a reaped child is a no-op, the way signalling our own reaped POSIX child is).
__destruct()Containment at teardown — and the POSIX asymmetry, named.

ConPtyMasterPty final class

The ConPTY master end: the pseudo console plus the two pipes that carry its side of the byte stream.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly ConPtyApi $api, private readonly int $pseudoConsole, array $inputPipe, array $outputPipe, int $cols, int $rows)
api(): ConPtyApiPackage seam: the slave adapter builds its CreateProcess call through the same binding, and the job/attribute handles only make sense next to this pseudo console.
pseudoConsole(): intPackage seam: the HPCON handle for ConPtySlavePty::spawn() and for ConPtySlavePty::path()'s label.
read(int $len = 8192, ?float $timeout = 0.05): ?stringRead up to $len bytes of child output.
write(string $bytes): intWrite to the child's input side of the pseudo console.
resize(int $cols, int $rows): voidForward the resize into the pseudo console (its ResizePseudoConsole leg), then keep the cache size() serves from.
size(): arrayThe last geometry set.
stream(): mixedThere is no PHP stream behind a ConPTY master — the pipes are Win32 handles the FFI binding holds, not stream resources — so this throws rather than pretending. Consequence callers must know: PosixPump, ReactPump and MultiPump stay POSIX-only; pump a ConPTY master with the bounded-timeout read() loop instead.
setBlocking(bool $blocking): void
fd(): intSame reason as stream(): a Win32 handle is not a file descriptor, and handing back a number that cannot cross the boundary would be a lie.
close(): voidIdempotent, total release: the master's pipe ends FIRST, then the pseudo console.
isClosed(): bool
